importer.py:46-47 _norm = ' '.join(text.split()).lower() (trim, collapse whitespace, casefold). doc_key (71-72) uses _norm on content; pair_key (67-68) uses _norm(question) plus sql_key. sql_key (50-64) returns ('parsed', regenerated mysql) only when sqlglot yields exactly one non-None statement; zero or multiple statements, or any exception, fall to ('text', sql.strip()), i.e. identical text after trimming. Stored and incoming entries both use these keys (lines 122-134). Matches the claim.

Traced re-import of a file whose items were all saved by a prior import. Save path stores items verbatim: save_tool_usage stores question and json.dumps({'sql': sql}) (agent_memory.py:239-247), save_text_memory stores content (agent_memory.py:439-444), and groups via group_metadata. store.dedup_entries (store.py:199-227) rebuilds every such row: a schema doc needs non-blank string content, a pair needs run_sql tool_name, non-empty sql and str question. Import validators (schema.py:55-59, 85-93, 119-122) reject blank question/sql/content and max_length bounds the size, so no validated item is stored in a form dedup_entries skips. In importer._plan (importer.py:114-161) the stored and incoming keys are computed by the same pair_key/doc_key from identical text. sql_key (importer.py:50-64) catches any exception, including RecursionError, and falls back to the stripped text. Both sides therefore get the same deterministic key. Groups are merged as a union and stored back sorted, so the second import's incoming groups are subsets of the stored groups: merged == target.groups, nothing counts as updated, and new_items stays empty. Within-file duplicates collapse to one target, and the sql_pair and schema_doc keys are kept separate. Absolute-claim input tried: a file with a RecursionError-raising SQL and a tagged duplicate pair; both stay idempotent. Residual edge cases do not break the claim as written: items that errored on the first save (reported as errors) get saved on retry, and a store changed between imports. A corrupt store raises MemoryCorruptionError rather than saving.

serialize_json (io.py:203-206) dumps the bundle with model_dump(exclude_none=True), so groups are exported. But import_bundle (importer.py:175-213) runs _plan (114-161), which keys every incoming pair by pair_key = (normalized question, sql_key(sql)) (50-68) and merges any item matching an earlier item of the same import into one record (lines 139-154: no new record, groups unioned). So two stored records that export as distinct entries but share a key, for example 'SELECT 1;' and 'SELECT 1' with the same question, which sqlglot MySQL regeneration makes identical, come back from an import into an empty store as ONE record with merged groups. Record count and per-entry group sets are not preserved, so the round trip is not lossless. Records stored before the sql_key rule can differ under the old rule but match under the new one, so this input is reachable. Separately, a tagged entry whose group no rule set lists makes the import raise UnknownMemoryGroupsError (193-195); docs/external/managing-memory.md:88 discloses that refusal, so it is a caveat, not the main counterexample. The doc claim at line 148, 'complete, lossless backup', is an absolute statement and is wrong for duplicate-under-key records.

I relied on pydantic v2 behaviour from knowledge, not on a run. Whitespace-only strings count as non-empty, which matches the claim's wording. criteria.json read; criterion 1 present and matches the claim. src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:394 declares RuleSet.memory_groups as list[NonEmptyStr] | None, default None, min_length=1. The validator at 396-401 calls _no_duplicates (line 66), which raises ValueError on a duplicate. Pydantic ValidationError is the same refusal path as other RuleSet fields. Omitting the key leaves None, so files without memory_groups load as before; memory_groups_for (754) and memory_groups (762) handle None. TOML (tomllib, line 837) cannot express null, so None comes only from omission. RuleSetFile._version (497-502) accepts only format_version == 1, and the file loads with memory_groups present under it. Trigger split: the code conditions are min_length, StrictStr, the duplicate check and the version check.
